ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18968, effective Nov 1, 2024) and the Enforcement Decree thereof; Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (Act No. 18969); Financial Services Commission Regulation on Identification and Verification of Real Beneficial Owners; Commercial Act (Act No. 17905) for corporate records; and the Supreme Court Registration Rules for company registry filings.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court Registry Office (법원등기소) under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by Korean court registry; notarized by a Korean notary public; then apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) of the Republic of Korea. For use in non-Apostille states, consular legalization by the Korean consulate of the destination country is required instead of apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (법인등기부등본 및 납세증명서)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court Registry Office and National Tax Service (NTS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain from Korean court registry and NTS; notarize; apostille via MOFA for Apostille Convention states; for non-member states, consular legalization by the destination country's consulate in Korea.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney (이사회 결의서 또는 위임장)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company's board of directors (notarized by a Korean notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the resolution or PoA; then apostille via MOFA for Apostille states; for non-Apostille states, consular legalization by the destination country's consulate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company founders or legal representative, notarized by a Korean notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the Articles; apostille via MOFA for Apostille states; for non-Apostille states, consular legalization by the destination country's consulate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank where the company maintains or will maintain an account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by the bank; notarized; apostille via MOFA for Apostille states; for non-Apostille states, consular legalization by the destination country's consulate.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) PEP list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the U.S. OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean government's own sanctions list (e.g., the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' list of designated persons). The screening must be performed at onboarding, on a continuous basis (at least daily), and upon any change in ownership or control. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for any PEP, including foreign PEPs, and for any entity with a high-risk jurisdiction nexus. The process must include name matching with fuzzy logic, alias detection, and verification of source of funds and wealth. All results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry Office Online Portal (IRO) – 법원등기소 인터넷등기소
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Korean (Hangul) and must include a legal form indicator such as '유한회사' (Yuhan Hoesa) or '주식회사' (Jusik Hoesa). An English transliteration may be used as a secondary name, but the Korean name is the official registered name. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names; phonetic similarity is considered. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing company, trademark, or well-known mark. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a distinctive element, (2) a business description, (3) a legal form suffix, and (4) optional additional identifiers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop), Act No. 1211, as amended, especially Articles 287 through 287-46 governing a yuhan hoesa (limited liability company), together with relevant provisions of the Civil Act, the Corporate Registration Rules, and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident subscribers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registry Office (Jibang Beobwon Deunggiso) - Registration Division (Deunggi-gwa) with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Formation Registration Application (Hoesa Seongnip Deunggi Sincheongseo) accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan), capital deposit certificate, and statutory attachments.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a yuhan hoesa. The stated capital in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully subscribed and the total contribution amount must be deposited into a preliminary bank account in the name of the company-in-organization before the formation registration is filed. The deposited funds remain blocked for the exclusive use of the company until registration is completed. When any subscriber is a non-resident, the subscription is subject to the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and must be reported to a designated foreign exchange bank or the Ministry of Economy and Finance, as applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) RESOLUTION NO. 2025-001 EFFECTIVE DATE [as inserted] THIS RESOLUTION is adopted by the first director of Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (the Act), and solely in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan). WHEREAS the Company will engage in computer programming, data processing, SEO data crawling, keyword analytics, SaaS platform operations, and related MarTech services; and WHEREAS the first director is required to effect the statutory incorporation and to authorize all pre-registration matters, including subscription for capital units, banking arrangements, registered office adoption, and officer appointments. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT OF CAPITAL. The total stated capital set forth in the Articles of Incorporation is hereby approved and subscribed. The first director is directed to open a preliminary capital collection account with a licensed bank in the name of the Company in organization, to receive the full amount of subscribed contributions, and to obtain a certificate of deposit. No contribution may be withdrawn before the Company formation registration is entered in the commercial register. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The opening of the Company's domestic and foreign currency operating accounts at licensed banks is approved. The representative director and any other officer designated by the first director are authorized to execute account opening forms, sign cheques, initiate electronic fund transfers, connect payment gateway providers Stripe and Paddle, and otherwise manage banking facilities. Each bank is entitled to rely on this resolution until notice of a superseding resolution is given. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office identified in the Articles of Incorporation is adopted. The first director shall procure the lease agreement, deliver the lessor's consent to the registration office, and file the registered office particulars with the district court and the National Tax Service. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The undersigned first director is appointed as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Company and is authorized to perform all duties required by law, including representation of the Company in industrial licensing, tax filings, and financial matters. An auditor shall be selected at the first members general meeting if required under the Act; until then, the representative director may exercise non-audit compliance functions. 5. GLOBAL AUTHORIZATION. The representative director is authorized to execute, sign, notarize, file, and deliver all documents, pay applicable registration duties, affix the corporate seal, issue certificates to banks, and take all lawful measures necessary to complete the Company's formation and commence the SEO analytics business. ADOPTED by the sole first director on the date set out above and recorded in the Company resolution book. This resolution shall not be revocable except by a subsequent unanimous members resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Preparation of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (Daebeobwon Deunggi-so, www.ireg.co.kr) and a Korean Notary Public for certification of signatures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators must conduct an exact Korean-language name search through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office and ensure that the proposed trade name Yuhan Hoesa and its English transliteration are not identical to any existing registered corporation in the same commercial register. The Articles of Incorporation must set out the corporate objective, corporate name, location of the registered office, total amount of equity capital, number and contribution amount of each capital unit, method of contribution, the name and passport or resident registration identification of each member, the method of publication, and the names of directors. Each incorporator or a foreign signatory must sign or affix a seal to the Articles, and where the applicant is a non-resident, the signature must be notarized or apostilled. The draft must be sent to a Korean notary public for certification if required by the registry. The applicant then reserves the name and preserves the name reservation certificate for the registration filing. If any statutory element is incomplete, the notary or registration clerk will flag the deficiency before submission, and the applicant must amend the Articles and re-execute them.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each incorporator
Apostille or notarized signature certificate for foreign members
Name reservation certificate or search result
Power of attorney for the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is queried or rejected, choose another non-conflicting name or obtain written consent from the existing name holder; then re-file the reservation in the same online portal. Corrections are processed immediately and do not restart the incorporation clock.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Foreign Investment Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Foreign Exchange Bank in Korea; for non-resident subscribers, the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the designated bank acting as receiving agent under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company-in-organization opens a temporary bank account in its provisional name. The representative director or the appointed agent deposits the full stated capital from the subscribers' own funds into the account. The bank issues a certificate of deposit or balance certificate that precisely identifies the company name, the deposit date, and the amount. If any subscriber is not a Korean resident, that subscriber must file a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act with a designated foreign exchange bank before or simultaneously with the capital deposit; the bank will verify the source of funds, ownership percentage, and declared value. The entire deposit must remain blocked until the court issues the corporate registration; no withdrawal is allowed during the formation period unless the registration is abandoned, in which case the deposit is returned to the subscribers under a written resolution. Any discrepancy between the exchange rate, the account name, or the deposit amount shall be rectified by the bank before proceeding.
required_dossiers: Wire transfer or cash deposit receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the balance certificate after the bank reconciles the account name or amount; if the Foreign Investment Promotion Act report contains errors, submit an adjustment report within the permitted period with a corrected ownership schedule and source of funds evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Formation Registration with the District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry Office - Registration Division (Deunggi-gwa) having territorial jurisdiction over the Company's registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of the capital deposit and notarization, the representative director or a duly authorized agent files the Company Formation Registration Application with the Registration Division of the district court having jurisdiction over the registered office. The application must include the exact corporate name, object, registered office, total contributed capital, the type and number of capital units subscribed by each member, names and resident identification of directors, and the method of representation. The court will verify that the Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, director acceptance, lease consent, and registration tax payment are genuine. After review, the court enters the company in the commercial register and issues the corporate register certificate, at which time the Yuhan Hoesa is legally incorporated. The applicant shall preserve the sealed registration register and all supporting papers for ten years. If the application is suspended, the court will issue a correction or supplementation order; the applicant must cure the defects within the grace period and re-submit the corrected form.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Follow the court's correction order and re-submit the corrected form; if the defect concerns the name or registered office, change the office or obtain a written consent from the prior name holder and file a new application, or seek an administrative remedy within 15 days of the rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Tax Office Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) District Tax Office with jurisdiction over the registered office, using the HomeTax online portal (www.hometax.go.kr).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days of company formation, the representative director must file a business registration application with the National Tax Service through HomeTax or at the local district tax office. The application must include the corporate register certificate, corporate seal certificate, lease contract, and representative personal identification. The tax office assigns the corporate business registration number and VAT registration number. For a data analytics and SEO tool under ISIC 6201, no additional industrial operating license is required; however, the tax office should be notified that the activity is an information technology service rather than a manufacturing shop. After issuance of the business registration certificate, the company must file simplified VAT returns on a quarterly basis and comply with the electronic tax invoice obligations under the Framework Act on National Taxes. If a supplementary data request is issued, respond with lease payment evidence and registered office photographs to verify that the location is an office, not a manufacturing or warehousing site.
required_dossiers: Business lease contract and lessor certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit the requested lease invoices, building ownership certificate, or office floor plan; if the tax office misclassifies the business type, file a correction to the business type code under ISIC 6201 and provide a written explanation that the activities are digital analytics services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal Registration, Bank Account Activation, and Payment Gateway KYB
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public for corporate seal registration; licensed domestic bank compliance department; Financial Supervisory Service for anti-money-laundering supervision; Stripe and Paddle merchant underwriting desk.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The representative director obtains a corporate seal and registers the seal certificate at the competent registry office or through a Korean notary. The company then presents the corporate register extract, the Articles of Incorporation, the corporate seal certificate, a board resolution approving bank accounts, and the representative director passport to the bank to convert the preliminary account into an active corporate operating account. The bank will complete anti-money-laundering and know-your-business due diligence, including the ultimate beneficial ownership declaration and the anticipated transaction volume for Stripe and Paddle merchant processing. Upon acceptance, the bank issues an account opening certificate which is forwarded to Stripe and Paddle to complete underwriting, fraud monitoring, and payout registration. If underwriting is rejected, the company must submit a corrected UBO declaration or a detailed business plan to the payment provider. The account should be configured with dual authorization for withdrawals above USD 5,000, and all banking and compliance correspondence must be retained in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Board resolution for banking and payment gateways
Anticipated transaction volume and business plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Appeal a KYB or payment gateway rejection through the bank compliance e-channel with an updated ownership chart, capital source statement, and customer contracts; if necessary, select a secondary licensed bank and repeat the onboarding process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity under ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx; ISIC 6201 is a pure digital service and does not require an industrial licensing board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - SEO content analytics and keyword analytics tool requires no industrial operating permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category Exempt - ISIC 6201 is a software and data-processing service; no Environmental Impact Assessment scoping or full EIA is required under the Korean Environmental Impact Assessment Act or the Act on Assessment of Impacts of Material EIA Objects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the office has no industrial point-source discharges, no VOC emissions, and no hazardous waste generation; disposal of exhausted computing equipment, batteries, and e-waste is governed by the Waste Control Act and the Act on the Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources, requiring separate collection and certified recycler transfer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for manufacturing operations; the company's leased office must nevertheless obtain the building owner's fire safety certificate and undergo the regular fire inspection of the National Fire Agency under the Fire-Fighting Installation and Maintenance Act. Workplace safety shall be managed under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including compliance with the General Safety Standards on Office Workplaces, and a written safety supervision plan prepared by the representative director.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; online portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity, the procedure to obtain a statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) is to apply for a Business Registration Number (BRN) with the NTS. The application can be submitted online via the HomeTax portal or in person at the local district tax office. Required documents include: certificate of incorporation, articles of association, passport of the legal representative, and a power of attorney if applicable. The BRN serves as the TIN for both corporate income tax and VAT purposes. For foreign suppliers of electronic services (including SaaS), a simplified registration process is available via HomeTax, requiring submission of the entity's details and appointment of a local tax representative if no permanent establishment exists in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Yuhan Hoesa is a standard limited liability company subject to corporate income tax; no check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections are available under Korean tax law for this entity type.)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For domestic businesses: KRW 80,000,000 annual turnover. For foreign suppliers of electronic services (including SaaS): KRW 10,000,000 annual sales to Korean customers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All B2B transactions require electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoice) issued and transmitted to the NTS via the HomeTax system within the prescribed deadline (by the 10th of the following month). For B2C transactions, cash receipts or electronic sales information must be reported. Foreign suppliers must also issue e-Tax Invoices for B2B sales to Korean customers. There is no real-time fiscal clearance, but the NTS performs automated cross-checking of invoices. Anti-fraud measures include digital stamping and encryption of e-Tax Invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated if the goods are physically exported from Korea and evidenced by a customs export declaration. Services (including digital services) are zero-rated if supplied to a non-resident and the benefit is enjoyed outside Korea. For SEO analytics SaaS, the supplier must retain evidence that the customer is a non-resident and that the service is not used in Korea. The zero-rating applies to B2B and B2C supplies to non-residents, provided the service is not effectively connected with a permanent establishment in Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or Foreign Exchange Bank Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without proper documentation or if foreign exchange is not repatriated within 180 days, the NTS may impose additional VAT, interest, and penalties up to 40% of the tax amount. Fraudulent claims may result in criminal prosecution and fines up to KRW 100 million.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the monetary authority, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) which exercises statutory administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won (KRW) is classified as a fully convertible currency for current account transactions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with the overwhelming majority of trade-related settlements free from quantitative restrictions. Capital account transactions, however, remain subject to a monitored liberalization regime: foreign direct investment, loans, and issuance of securities must be reported through designated foreign exchange banks; prior filing or approval is required for certain categories. There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds into KRW; exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic foreign currency accounts without conversion obligation. Profit remittance, including dividends and royalties, is generally permissible provided that the underlying transaction is evidenced and tax compliance verified (with certificate of withholding taxes). The MOEF and BOK impose ex-post reporting and statistical collection requirements rather than exchange controls, but deviations from the declared business purpose or trade documentation can trigger immediate on-site inspections and asset freeze action under the criminal provisions of FETA. For a foreign-invested LLC engaged in SEO content analytics, the most material hurdles are not convertibility limits but documentary strictness in capital verification, the five-year foreign exchange reporting history required of the designated bank, and mandatory electronic submission through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). Given the firm's MarTech SaaS nature and expected outbound licensing revenue, the classification of platform-based service fees as either goods or services can materially alter the surrender timeline and the procurement of an export certificate from the Korea Customs Service.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 12 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds for general merchandise and digital services must be received within 6 months from the export declaration date; the deadline may be extended by the designated foreign exchange bank if the exporter demonstrates justifiable grounds (e.g., deferred payment terms) for up to an additional 6 months. There is no mandatory statutory conversion ratio to KRW; all export receipts may be held in foreign currency accounts at domestic banks without surrender, but the exporter must file a transaction statement with the designated bank and report the inward remittance within 30 days. For digital content analytics subscriptions treated as cross-border provision of services, exporters are expected to maintain an export invoice with a Korea Origin Certificate or a digital service contract to prove the underlying real transaction and avoid misclassification penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW) + Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR/JPY)
Capital Escrow Account (for FDI verification) + Operational Settlement Account
Primary Treasury Account (KRW) with trade finance and FX hedging facilities
Cross-border transaction account with dedicated Foreign Investment Support Desk
Operational Account for domestic payments and payroll

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Overseas fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Wise, Revolut, or Airwallex are legally barred from acting as full-service deposit-taking or settlement banks in Korea because they do not hold a banking license under the Banking Act nor a crypto- or electronic-money license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. These EMIs cannot provide a domestic KRW IBAN that is cleared through Korea's financial system (KOFI or J-Inet) nor can they accept inbound wire transfers intended for tax compliance under FIPA. At best, an offshore EMI can be used as a non-Korean, segregated collection vehicle outside Korea for foreign customers; however, remittance of those proceeds into the Korean LLC will still trigger the same FX reporting requirements and designated-bank routing. Therefore, the entity must maintain its primary settlement and treasury accounts at a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank. The strategic recommendation is to use Stripe and Paddle as upstream billing portals, but to auto-route daily settlements via API into a Woori or Shinhan KRW operational account, thereby preserving the valid bank channel for tax and FX compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) with one or more non-resident shareholders/directors, South Korea's Financial Action Task Force-aligned Know Your Customer regulations and the Real-Name Financial Transaction Act mandate that at least one beneficial owner or statutory director with actual authority appear in-person at the branch of the designated foreign exchange bank for a face-to-face interview and ID verification. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted for fully non-resident entities; a power of attorney executed at a Korean consulate may be accepted for the signing of account documents only after the director's first in-branch visit. As an alternative, a non-resident director can complete the physical identification at a Korean branch of a global bank if that branch is the same institution (e.g., Shinhan Bank in New York is not sufficient; the Korean branch is required). For efficiency, the proposed LLC should appoint a local resident representative (not necessarily a shareholder) to handle the in-branch appearance, while the non-resident founder provides notarized corporate resolutions and a board resolution appointing the representative as legal signatory. The bank's compliance committee may additionally require an official visit to the registered office if the registered seat is a shared office, to verify actual business substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unresolved beneficial ownership chain due to multiple layers of offshore holding companies or nominee shareholders involved in a newly formed Korean LLC
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full corporate ownership chart, certified copies of the Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum from each intermediary holding entity, HKMA/FCA/Austrian equivalent certification of the beneficial owner's passport, a notarized trust declaration if any ownership is held through a trust, and a written explanation of the economic substance of each layer. Include also a P.A.S.S. / PEP screening clear result for every shareholder, alongside an external counsel opinion stating that no nominee or sham entity is present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to demonstrate the lawful source of the initial capital contribution from a non-resident shareholder into the Korean LLC capital escrow account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the shareholder's corporate audited financial statements for the last three fiscal years, executive tax clearance, bank statements showing the exact funding source (e.g., accumulated profits, liquidation dividend, or proceeds from a business sale), and a sworn declaration of source of funds. If the contribution is derived from personal crypto-asset gains, a full transaction history and valuation report from a certified independent valuer must be attached, because Korean banks uniformly reject crypto-to-fiat transfers of this nature without forensic audit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A mismatch between the declared marketing/business scope (ISIC 6201 computer programming) and the actual revenue trail from Stripe/Paddle digital subscription transactions including cross-border payments from sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed revenue waterfall report from Stripe/Paddle mirroring each subscription end-user country, along with the commercial contracts and customer invoices, and a country-blocking policy statement confirming the LLC does not accept users from OFAC sanctioned territories. The bank will require a written compliance memo from the vendor's compliance team and a self-certification that the platform is not exploited by sanctioned third parties. Additionally, the Korean entity must submit its annual business substance declaration evidencing actual development activities, employee role descriptions, and server expenses in Korea.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid expected transaction volume in the first month after account opening that appears disproportionate to the declared paid-in capital, creating an alarming velocity-of-funds pattern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a treasury forecast model in Korean-language format showing monthly revenue projections, conversion rates, and expected average ticket size based on the MarTech analytics SaaS benchmark. Include executed partnership agreements with two seed customers, a board-approved three-year spending plan, and a tax accountant's letter confirming the projected corporation tax and VAT (VAT on e-services) obligations. Highlight that the company has no accrued debt and that the revenue swings are typical of a global SaaS platform, and attach evidence of the company's payment card processing agreement with Stripe and Paddle to demonstrate their respective AML protections.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital contributions for a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa must be routed through a designated foreign exchange bank (DFEB) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and reported to the MOEF (practically delegated to applicable ministries). The procedure is: (a) the foreign investor reports the proposed foreign direct investment to the MOEF before fund transfer via the FEIS system, specifying the FIPA purpose code 'CAPITAL_INVEST_IN_KOREA'; (b) the investor transfers the capital from its offshore bank account to the DFEB's foreign currency account opened in the name of the Korean LLC, denominated in USD or KRW, using SWIFT MT103/202. The remittance must include a precise narrative with the taxpayer identification number (KR LLC business registration number) and the reference to the FDI report registration number. Upon receipt, the DFEB issues a Foreign Currency Inward Remittance Certificate and converts the funds to KRW at the inter-bank spot rate as per instruction. The capital verification certificate is generated by the DFEB and must be registered with the court registry of the LLC within two months; after verification, the funds are freed from escrow and can be transferred to the operational KRW account. Inbound payment for working capital other than FDI (e.g., shareholder loans) requires separate notification to the MOEF under the 'borrowing' section; the total outstanding loan is subject to a 50 million KRW minimum threshold before approval. For the SEO analytics tool, dividend repatriation will follow the same rail with the route 'SECURITIES_CAPITAL_GAINS_DIVIDEND_DOMESTIC_REMITTANCE' and must be accompanied by a certified statement of distributable profits from the external auditor.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound disbursements to global SaaS vendors, subcontractors, and advertising partners, the preferred clearing rails in Korea are (1) SWIFT MT103 for straightforward vendor payments and subscription fees, settled through the DFEB with the remittance purpose code 'PAYMENT_FOR_SERVICES' (click-stream data procurement, cloud computing costs) and 10% domestic VAT withholding consideration where applicable; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (sight or usance) for any hardware or dedicated server purchases from overseas dealers, valid under the UCP 600 rules issued by the Korean bank and typically requiring a pro forma invoice, transport document, and compliance certificate; (3) Documentary Collections (CAD / D/P) for pragmatic settlements with emerging-market partners in the content analytics ecosystem where contracts are established but L/C costs are unjustifiable; (4) Cross-border payroll and contractor payments via standard bank transfers with the purpose code 'LABOR_COST_ABROAD_PAYMENT', supported by employment contracts and evidence of tax residence (W-8BEN / CNI / NRIC). All outward payments must be recorded in the FEIS and the bank's periodic reporting obligation to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit will trigger additional scrutiny if the beneficiary is in a financially lenient or sanctioned jurisdiction. It is imperative to maintain a full reconciliation subsystem inside the enterprise resource planning software that maps each outgoing transfer to the corresponding inbound revenue stream, thereby proving that the movement of funds is aligned with the firm's declared business plan and is not a disguised currency swap.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD Forward FX Contracts with a licensed designated foreign exchange bank, restricted to hedging 120% of the underlying trade receivables evidenced by a valid purchase order or contract.

FX Options (European style, call/put) on KRW/USD, permissible for hedging anticipated subscription revenue cash flows, with the notional amount capped at the firm's average four-quarter projected revenue reported to the tax office.
Cross-Currency Swaps only for larger capital financing / loan rollovers; permissible where the swap tenor matches the underlying FX loan and all payments are run through the firm's DFEB.

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for onshore Korean companies under the FETA except when the transaction has an underlying real capital-account exposure approved by the MOEF; therefore, the entity should enter only onshore deliverable forwards and avoid accessing the NDF market, as unauthorized NDF use may constitute a criminal act and invalidate the hedging protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and payment for the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the Hometax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the year following the fiscal year end (or within 3 months after the end of a non-calendar fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax; underreporting penalty of 10% of the understated amount; unfaithful declaration penalty of 10% of the unreported income; overdue payment interest of 0.025% per day on unpaid tax. Persistent non-payment permits compulsory tax collection, asset seizure, and, after statutory warnings, administrative closure of the business registration (de facto strike-off of the entity's active status).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return and payment (local surtax on national corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government (Si/Gun/Gu) through the Wetax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the national corporate income tax return: March 31 (or within 3 months from the end of a non-calendar fiscal year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax penalty, overdue interest on unpaid local income tax, asset seizure and administrative closure measures under the Framework Act on Local Taxes if payment remains outstanding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of members and formal approval of financial statements (internal corporate act; no external filing for a private LLC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate head office records; no external receiving authority for a private Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the fiscal year end, unless the articles of incorporation require an earlier date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting or to approve the financial statements may make directors personally liable for resulting losses, and ordinary fines may be imposed under the Korean Commercial Act. Repeated failure may be treated as evidence for administrative closure of the business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and audited financial statements (applicable only if the mandatory audit thresholds are met or an audit is voluntarily elected)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS); the auditor files the audit report through the FSS electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks after the date of the auditor's report; in any event, the audited financial statements must be laid before the general meeting within 6 months after the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violation of the Act on External Audit of Corporations may result in administrative corrective orders, fines up to KRW 30,000,000 (approximately USD 22,200) and sanctions against the auditor. A knowingly false audit report may also create criminal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual regular report of a foreign-invested enterprise (if a non-resident investor holds at least 10% of the equity or management control under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through the Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the year following the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act of up to KRW 5,000,000 (approximately USD 3,700), loss of foreign investment status and related incentives, and reassessment of capital transaction benefits.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit of Corporations, an independent certified public accountant audit is mandatory for a Yuhan Hoesa if, at the preceding fiscal year end, total assets equal or exceed KRW 50 billion (approximately USD 37 million). A mandatory audit is also triggered when total assets equal or exceed KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.4 million) and either (i) annual sales revenue equals or exceeds KRW 30 billion (approximately USD 22 million) or (ii) the average number of employees during the fiscal year is 100 or more. Listed companies, companies subject to consolidated external audit supervision, and other entities designated by the Financial Services Commission are audited regardless of asset size. For a below-threshold LLC, audit is elective; if elected, the audit must be performed under the same statutory CPA independence and reporting standards.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS is mandatory for companies that are required to apply K-IFRS under securities market rules and for designated large entities. A private Yuhan Hoesa may prepare its financial statements under general Korean GAAP (Korean Accounting Standards) or K-IFRS for SMEs. If an external audit is statutorily required, the financial statements must present a true and fair view in accordance with the applicable framework, and the audit must follow the audit standards established by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no standalone annual UBO confirmation obligation for a Korean private LLC within the ordinary commercial-law framework. However, if the entity is a foreign-invested enterprise under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, it must file an annual regular report on investment and ownership structure to MOTIE/KOTRA by March 31 after the fiscal year end. Shareholding transfers must be reflected in the member register and filed with the Commercial Registry within 14 days of the transfer. In a foreign-invested company context, an amendment report is also required within 30 days under FIPA.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Directors' Register, where the LLC has directors)
Register of Charges/Mortgages (if any security is granted over the company's assets)
Minute Book of Meetings of Members and Directors

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - 3,500 per year for a compliant registered office address plus company secretarial administrative assistance in Seoul; USD 700 - 1,500 per year for a regional outsourced registered address with basic mail handling.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 12,000 for an independent CPA audit of a small or medium private LLC with assets below KRW 50 billion; fees of USD 25,000 - 60,000 or more may apply at the mandatory audit threshold.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Progressive CIT: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME corporate tax deductions, R&D tax credits for software/algorithm development, foreign-invested company tax incentives in free economic zones or foreign investment zones, and technology transfer income tax exemptions; no specific patent-box regime applies to pure SaaS, but R&D credits materially reduce the effective rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Payable Calculation Statement (Corporate Tax Return) filed electronically via the National Tax Service HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) e-filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., 31 March for a 31 December year-end); semi-annual corporate tax prepayments are due within 3 months after the end of each half-year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Company Identification and Legal Representative
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate registration number, legal entity name, registered address, place of effective management, and representative or statutory agent identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State whether the company is a domestic corporation subject to worldwide taxation or a foreign corporation with a Korean establishment subject to Korean-source taxation only. If the legal representative or shareholder is a non-resident, list nationality and tax residence; attach the power of attorney for a local tax representative when the non-resident is not present in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from all business activities, including SaaS subscriptions, SEO analytics licensing, data crawler service fees, and export sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report accrued revenue in KRW using the Bank of Korea exchange rate. Do not net Stripe or Paddle processing fees; record gross turnover and claim payment-processing fees as deductible expenses. Export income qualifies for any zero-rating or export incentive only after documentary proof of foreign exchange receipt is maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Taxable Income (Tax Base) After Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net book income adjusted for non-taxable income, non-deductible expenses, depreciation, carried-forward losses, and transfer-pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recompute transactions with foreign related parties at arm's length. Excessive management fees, royalties, or interest paid to a non-resident parent or licensor must be disallowed if unsupported by contemporaneous documentation. Include foreign-source income of a domestic corporation and claim foreign tax credits separately. For a Yuhan Hoesa with non-resident shareholders, any suppressed revenue linked to unreported foreign-held payment accounts must be added to the tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Corporate Tax at Progressive Rates and Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed national corporate income tax after applying statutory brackets and allowable credits such as R&D credits and temporary investment tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits are subject to separate carryforward restrictions, generally 5 years. If the R&D project benefits a foreign related party, ensure the service is commercially relevant and that arm's-length compensation has been recognized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Local Income Tax Surcharge and Special Surcharges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of the national corporate tax payable and any additional penalties or interest related to the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate shareholders are not directly assessed on the local surcharge at entity level, but the surcharge is not reduced by tax treaties and must be paid by the Korean company before profit repatriation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Withholding Tax on Amounts Paid to Non-Residents
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of dividends, interest, royalties, and other income paid or credited to non-resident shareholders, creditors, and licensors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each non-resident payee and tax residence. Self-assess statutory 22% withholding tax, consisting of 20% national tax plus 2% local surcharge, unless treaty relief is approved. Attach valid Tax Residency Certificates and beneficial ownership declarations. If no treaty relief is claimed, remit the withheld amounts to the National Tax Service within the statutory deadlines; failure to withhold makes the company and its directors liable for unpaid tax plus penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing triggers a 20% surcharge on the unreported corporate tax and monthly delay interest at approximately 0.6%; unfaithful understatement may attract a 40% omission penalty under the Framework Act on Taxes. Fraudulent evasion is punishable under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act by imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine up to twice the evaded tax, plus personal collection against directors and travel bans.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on cash or deemed dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, composed of 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Korean payer must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, together with a beneficial ownership statement and, where applicable, evidence of shareholding percentage and holding period. The payer then files an Application for Non-Resident Withholding Tax Reduction or Exemption with the National Tax Service before or at the time of payment. The foreign recipient must not be a conduit; absent timely and compliant documentation, the statutory 22% rate must be withheld. Retroactive relief may be available through tax adjustment but remains subject to statute-of-limitations rules and anti-abuse review under limitation-on-benefits and principal-purpose tests.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 22%, composed of 20% national tax plus 2% local surcharge. Most Korean bilateral treaties reduce interest to approximately 10% to 15% and royalties to 10% to 15%, with possible 0% treaty treatment for certain software copyright transfers if the beneficial owner meets the treaty definition of royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10 billion in cross-border related-party transactions for the same fiscal year, combined with global consolidated revenue of at least KRW 100 billion, triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation. Smaller intercompany transactions still require annual international transaction schedules and contemporaneous documentation when the amount exceeds approximately KRW 100 million per related counterparty.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the National Tax Service examines substance through the OECD general anti-avoidance rule, beneficial ownership analysis, and the place-of-effective-management test. A Yuhan Hoesa that is managed from abroad, lacks a domestic board seat, or performs no Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea may be reclassified as a foreign tax-resident or lose treaty benefits. Such a shell-corporation structure may also trigger controlled-foreign-company rules and director liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating Stripe or Paddle accounts in foreign countries and using them to collect SEO-tool subscription revenue without recording the income in the Korean corporate tax return, or understating revenue by netting payment-processor fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine not exceeding twice the evaded tax; additionally, an unfaithful tax return surcharge of 40% of the underreported amount plus 0.6% monthly delay interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who participated in concealment or failed to exercise supervisory duty is jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax and penalties. Criminal conviction may result in disqualification from serving as a director, seizure of personal assets, and a travel ban imposed by the National Tax Service during investigation and collection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Shell Company Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming a Korean Yuhan Hoesa with no office, no employees, no local management, and no independent decision-making, then paying inflated management fees or royalties to a related offshore entity to shift profits out of Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing adjustment under Article 4 of the International Tax Coordination Act, with a penalty surcharge of up to 20% of the adjusted tax amount. Failure to submit a Local File or Master File is penalized per unfiled document, and a wrongfully claimed treaty benefit may be denied in full.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts pierce the corporate veil when the company is a mere alter ego, making the foreign parent, shareholder, and local director personally liable for adjusted tax and penalties. Fraudulent intercompany documentation can result in criminal investigation for obstruction of tax collection, with possible imprisonment up to 5 years and a travel ban until liabilities are settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Foreign Financial Account Reporting Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding funds or payment proceeds in overseas processor accounts such as Stripe or Paddle and failing to declare the aggregate foreign bank or security account balance when it exceeds KRW 500 million at year-end, while also disguising account ownership through a non-resident nominee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 16 of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Information authorizes a penalty of up to 20% of the unreported balance and a criminal fine of up to KRW 50 million. Repeat violations can trigger aggravated imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act when linked to tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director is individually criminally liable if the foreign account belongs to the corporation but is controlled personally. Sanctions include confiscation of hidden funds, imprisonment up to 5 years, personal asset seizure for restitution, and placement on the immigration blacklist preventing overseas business travel until disclosure and tax liabilities are resolved.
